Du analysierst die Performance unserer Beiträge und leitest daraus Optimierungen und neue Content-Ideen ab. Creator- & UGC-Management Du steuerst die Zusammenarbeit mit unseren Creatorn: Briefing, Kommunikation, Timings und Abnahme laufen über dich. Du organisierst den Content-Workflow und stellst sicher, dass Creator-Content vollständig, pünktlich und einsatzbereit für Social, Performance Marketing und weitere Produktionen bereitsteht. Du pflegst unser Creator-Netzwerk und findest gemeinsam mit dem Team neue Gesichter, die zu NEOLYMP passen. Content-Produktion: Shootings & KI Du bist bei unseren Shootings vor Ort dabei, koordinierst Creator und Persönlichkeiten vor der Kamera und sorgst dafür, dass aus einem Drehtag möglichst viel verwertbarer Content entsteht. Du arbeitest im Content-Team an Workflows, in denen KI-Tools Recherche, Ideation, Schnitt oder Varianten-Erstellung beschleunigen – und bringst eigene Ideen ein, wie sich echter und KI-gestützter Content am besten ergänzen. Ein sicheres Gespür für Plattformen, Formate und Trends – und die Fähigkeit, sie markengerecht einzusetzen, statt jedem Hype hinterherzulaufen. Organisationstalent: Du koordinierst mehrere Creator und Produktionen parallel, hältst Timings ein und behältst den Überblick, auch wenn viel gleichzeitig läuft. Kommunikationsstärke: Du briefst klar, gibst Feedback wertschätzend und direkt und stimmst dich eng mit Marketing, Grafik und Performance ab. Ein grundlegendes Verständnis dafür, wie Content entlang der Customer Journey zum Verkauf beiträgt. Das zählt für uns am meisten Lust auf Content, Neugier auf neue Tools und die Motivation, mit der Rolle und dem Team zu wachsen. Die nächsten Schritte machen wir gemeinsam – dafür ist uns Drive wichtiger als das perfekte Profil. B. für Text, Bild oder Video). Erste Berührungspunkte mit Performance Marketing oder E-Commerce. Du erfüllst nicht jeden Punkt? Bewirb dich trotzdem. Job Description The Senior Planner is responsible for developing, maintaining, monitoring, and analysing project programmes across transportation projects, including rail, roads, highways, bridges, tunnels, and associated infrastructure. The role will support Project Managers and Project Controls teams in establishing realistic baseline programmes, monitoring actual progress, identifying schedule risks and delays, forecasting completion dates, and supporting timely corrective actions. Analyse the impact of delays, scope changes, late approvals, design changes, and interface constraints. Develop recovery and mitigation programmes in coordination with Project Managers and discipline leads. Undertake scenario planning and schedule sensitivity analysis where required. Brantford General Hospital – Our acute care hospital offering a full spectrum of inpatient and outpatient services. The Willett in Paris – Home to our urgent care centre and transitional care services, supporting patients through every step of their healthcare journey. With Over 130 Years Of Service, BCHS Is Evolving With a Renewed Focus On Excellence, Collaboration, And Innovation. Our Strategic Priorities Center On Quality Care, Connected Teams, And a Healthy Future For Our Patients, Our People, And Our Community. Our Culture Is Shaped By Our Core Values And Pillars Core Values: Be Bold and Courageous | Commit to Excellence | Champion Equity | Be Trustworthy Four Pillars: Patient-First | People-Centred | Partnership-Based | Progress-Focused These values reflect who we are, what we stand for, and how we work together to have influence. Join us in shaping the future of healthcare—right here at BCHS. Why Choose BCHS? Investing in You – Access to a centralized Education Fund, tuition support, and professional development opportunities. Flexible Scheduling – Within a standard work week Career Growth – Internal job postings, mentorship programs, and leadership development. Predictable Work Locations – Stability and consistency in your work environment. Collaborative Team Culture – Work alongside skilled professionals in a supportive, interdisciplinary setting. Employee Wellness Matters – Peer Support Team, Wellness Committee, Free, confidential Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for employees and their families. Commitment to Safety – Comprehensive safety programs for all Competitive Compensation and Benefits –– Salaries and benefits designed to align with industry standards, reinforcing our commitment to attracting and retaining top talent. Excellent Pension Plan. Diversity & Inclusion – We are actively working to diversify our teams and remove systemic barriers in hiring, retention, and advancement. We track and report on our progress because representation matters. We regularly review our benefits, policies, and programs through an equity lens to meet the needs of our diverse teams. Provide accommodations for religious practices and use trauma-informed policies that support mental wellbeing. Recognition & Rewards – Employee appreciation programs and professional recognition opportunities and Corporate Committee Community Impact – Make a real difference in patient care and public health every day. Choose Civility – Where every interaction matters. Civility and respect shape our workplace, as individuals treat one another—and the communities we serve with dignity, empathy, and cultural awareness. We foster a culture of civility by raising awareness, setting clear expectations, and continually reviewing our policies and practices to ensure respect is at the core of everything we do. Position Summary The Critical Care Unit is an intensivist-lead closed model with a dedicated Respiratory Therapy Team. Our CCU nurses actively support our RN-lead Critical Care Response Team throughout the hospital and have opportunities for involvement in research projects and continuing education. Reporting to the Clinical Manager, Critical Care, and the successful applicant will be responsible for providing evidenced based, comprehensive, safe, effective and ethical nursing care to all clients in need of Critical Care Services. Mandatory Qualifications Graduate of an accredited college or university nursing program Minimum 1 (One) year of Current experience on a Critical Care Unit Current Basic Cardiac Life Support (BCLS) certification Current Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS) certification Critical Care Certificate Program or an equivalent- completed or currently enrolled Ability to work in a Critical Care Response Team (CCRT) capacity preferred Core Competencies Demonstrated ability to work within a Total Patient Care Delivery system in which regulated health care professionals practice to their full scope adhering to the practice standards as defined by the College of Nurses of Ontario Proven critical thinking skills, creative problem solver with a solution focus and patient centered approach Demonstrated ability to communicate and use effective interpersonal skills with colleagues and other members of the BCHS and external partners Ability to multi task and set priorities in a high intensity and rapidly changing environment Demonstrated competence in patient assessment and care planning including but not limited to: Completion of comprehensive (systems based) patient assessments, identification and prioritization of critical patient needs, collaborative care planning with clients and families, implementation of nursing interventions, delegated medical acts, evaluation and documentation. Ensuring a discharge plan is part of the individualized plan of care Engaging patient and family in health teaching to achieved desired patient outcomes Demonstrated ability to interpret cardiac arrhythmias, describe their hemodynamic consequences and usual treatment approaches Demonstrated knowledge of life saving medications, intravenous vasoactive medications, paralytic agents, as well as general drug dosage calculation, administration of continuous medication infusions (such as but not limited to titrated vasoactive agents, platelet inhibitors, antiarrhythmic agents, thrombolytics, and insulin) and patient monitoring for medication effects Demonstrated ability to recognize the signs and symptoms of cardiopulmonary emergencies and initiation of advanced interventions to stabilize a patient. Demonstrated competencies in phlebotomy, IV initiation as well as care for central lines Demonstrated technical competencies in effective use of associated equipment including, but not limited to: Assisting with the initiation of life saving procedures such as, intubation, airway management, defibrillation, external pacing, and trans venous pacing. Effective management of airway support including mechanical ventilation IV Infusion pumps, oxygen delivery systems, telemetry packs, glucometers, non invasive blood pressure, specialty beds and overlay mattresses, closed chest tube drainage systems, and wound management systems, and transduced pressure lines (e.g., CVP, Arterial) Physically capable of performing the full scope of responsibilities Reliable individual with excellent attendance record and able to work all shifts, including weekends and holidays Demonstrated competence with Wound Vac Systems Self directed individual with the ability to work both independently and in partnership with members of the inter professional team Demonstrated commitment to continuing education and personal development in nursing Demonstrated negotiation and conflict resolution skills Ability to be a coach, teacher and mentor to colleagues and students Reliable individual with excellent attendance record and able to work all shifts Our Commitment to Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion BCHS is committed to building an inclusive and accessible workplace that reflects the diversity of the communities we serve. We welcome people from all walks of life, including people of all genders, sexual orientations, racial and ethnic backgrounds, Indigenous identities, abilities, and lived experiences. Inclusion is part of how we deliver better care We are dedicated to removing barriers and providing accommodations at every stage of the hiring process in accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA). If you require any accommodations, please inform us when contacted, and we will work with you to meet your needs. Ready to Make a Difference? If you are passionate about healthcare and looking for a supportive and dynamic work environment, we would love to hear from you! Apply today and join BCHS in delivering exceptional care with compassion and integrity. review_candidates.title: Project Technical Officer, Tonga
review_candidates.description: Location: Tonga City: Nuku'alofa Contract Type: Staff Grade: G8 Salary scale: International Scale End date of appointment 24 months Deadline: 20/10/2026 Job Reference: New-RP26-115 Please note that the deadline is based on Korean Standard Time Zone (KST, UTC+9) INTRODUCTION TO GGGI The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) is a treaty-based international, inter-governmental organization dedicated to supporting and promoting strong, inclusive and sustainable economic growth in developing countries and emerging economies. To learn more please visit about GGGI web page. BACKGROUND The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI), in partnership with the Tonga Department of Climate Change (DCC) under the Ministry of Meteorology, Energy, Information, Disaster Management, Environment, Climate Change and Communications (MEIDECC) is co-executing the delivery of Tonga’s first Biannual Transparency Report (BTR), with financial support from the Global Environment Facility (GEF) and the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) as the GEF Implementing Agency. The project aims to ensure Tonga delivers it’s first BTR meeting the standards set out in the Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF) under the Paris Agreement. The project will work closely with GGGI’s support under the Capacity Building for Improved Transparency (CBIT) project to address key barriers identified in Tonga's national communications, including inadequate institutional arrangements, lack of robust data management systems, and insufficient capacity and awareness among stakeholders. Position Summary The Project Technical Officer (PTO) role is to fulfil the full implementation of Tonga’s first Biennial Transparency Report (BTR). He/she will be responsible for the overall management of all aspects of the project and will provide technical assistance to the National Thematic Working Groups (TWGs). The PTO should have experience in the preparation of National Communications on Climate Change and/or in other climate change enabling activities such as Biennial Update Reports and/or Biennial Transparency Reports to the UNFCCC. He/she should have the ability to work with a wide variety of people from governments, agencies, non-governmental organizations, and research institutions is essential. The officer will be also contributing to the management of other relevant climate project as well as business development of the GGGI Tonga program. The candidate should be highly motivated, enthusiastic, and capable of working independently. The Project Technical Officer will oversee the day-to-day management, coordination, technical quality assurance, stakeholder engagement, and timely delivery of Tonga’s climate transparency reporting outputs. The role will support national Thematic Working Groups, coordinate inputs across key technical components, and ensure project activities and reports meet UNEP, UNFCCC, IPCC, ETF, and GEF requirements. PURPOSE The role exists to provide overall technical and project management leadership for implementation of the BTR project in Tonga. It contributes substantively by coordinating national inputs, supporting data collection and analysis, reviewing, and editing technical chapters, ensuring alignment with IPCC guidelines and UNFCCC reporting requirements, and strengthening the quality, transparency, and completeness of national climate reports. The work is broad and complex, covering greenhouse gas inventories, NDC tracking, adaptation, support needed and received, gender and climate change, reporting compilation, validation, and preparation for subsequent BTR and/or NC reporting. ENGAGEMENT The Project Technical Officer will work closely with UNEP, the Project Steering Committee, national Thematic Working Groups, relevant ministries, national and international research institutions, NGOs, consultants, and other partners. The role requires regular coordination, consultation, information sharing, workshop facilitation, and collaboration to mobilize expertise, gather and disseminate information, build national capacity, and ensure smooth implementation of project activities. DELIVERY The Project Technical Officer, in consultation with the Project Steering Committee, will be responsible for the day-to-day management, coordination and supervision of the implementation of the project. Support with technical components of the project will include the following: Component 1: Under the National Inventory Report chapter: Provide inputs on the draft of national circumstances and institutional arrangements for GHGI, coordinate data collection for GHG inventory calculations across 5 IPCC sectors, organize and facilitate stakeholder consultations, conduct training and workshops, and review the final compiled NIR. Component 2: Under the NDC Tracking chapter: Provide input on the draft of national circumstances and institutional arrangements for NDC tracking, organize and facilitate stakeholder consultations, contribute to the training, and workshops, review final compiled report on NDC tracking. Component 3: Under the chapter on Adaptation: Provide input on the draft of national circumstances and institutional arrangements for Component 3 (Climate impact and adaptation), support in identifying impacts, risks, and vulnerabilities, organize and facilitate stakeholder consultations, contribute to training, and workshops, conduct review of final compiled report on climate impact and adaptation. Under Component 4, draft chapter for information on financial, technology development and transfer and capacity-building, organize and help facilitate stakeholder consultations, training, and workshops, review and provide feedback on drafts and revisions, identify gaps, applicable flexibility and draft their related explanation. Under Component 5, support the compilation of information on gender and climate change and provide guidance to the Gender Specialist. Under Component 6, conduct inception and validation workshops, compile and format national reports, undertake a technical editing of the report, and draft an executive summary. Under Component 7, compile a stocktaking report for the preparation of the project proposal for subsequent BTR and/or BTR/NC report(s). Ensure quality assurance of data and align reports with IPCC guidelines. Ensure compliance with international climate reporting requirements (Modalities, Procedures and Guidelines (MPGs) - 18/CMA.1) Manage stakeholder engagement and ensure transparency throughout the reporting process. Address technical challenges to ensure accurate and timely submission of the BTR. Enhance clarity and completeness of the information provided to meet the standards of Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF). Contribute to the management and development of the GGGI Tonga programme with a focus on climate mitigation and resilience initiatives. Project Management Duties Will Include, Among Others Coordinate all project activities with heads of TWGs, and a range of institutions and agencies, including UNEP, IPCC, UNFCCC secretariat, GEF, and national institutions to ensure smooth and appropriate execution of project activities Prepare a detailed project workplan and terms of reference for the project consultants Liaise with the relevant ministries, national and international research institutes, NGOs, and other relevant institutions to involve their staff in the project activities, and to gather and disseminate information relevant to the project. Identify, interview and recruit national and international consultants to work for the project. Promote and establish links with related national and regional projects, and other international programs. Prepare the periodic progress reports on project implementation and ensure that all national project outputs are sent to UNEP. Manage the project expenditure according to the project budget. Identify training needs of the contracted national consultants and other project stakeholders and identify appropriate courses and training for national capacity building. Organize national workshops and training courses according to the project workplan. Attend, whenever possible, the relevant regional and international workshops, training courses and conferences. Review all materials generated during the project. Ensure the publication and dissemination of the reports identified as project outputs. Coordinate negotiations on co-operation with Government and financing institutions to identify and mobilize sources for the follow-up activities. Provide oversight and support for the effective management and implementation of other GGGI Tonga projects, as required. Requirements QUALIFICATIONS An advanced degree (at least MSc. or Ph.D.) in environmental science or another related field Over five years of experience in the field of climate change Familiarity with national communications, and with international negotiations and processes under the UNFCCC and Paris Agreement Substantial experience in government and in interdepartmental procedures He/she should have a strong scientific/technical and policy background. Familiarity with computers and world processing Good command of national and UN official language FUNCTIONAL The Project Technical Officer should demonstrate strong technical knowledge of climate change reporting, including greenhouse gas inventories, NDC tracking, adaptation, support needed and received, gender and climate change, and preparation of BTR and/or NC reports. The role requires the ability to apply IPCC, UNFCCC, ETF and GEF reporting requirements; coordinate data collection and analysis; review and edit technical reports; identify gaps and flexibility needs; and communicate substantive technical issues clearly to government, technical working groups, consultants, partners and other stakeholders. CORPORATE The Project Technical Officer’s Oversight Will Be Monitored Through Established Project Governance And Reporting Mechanisms. Specifically, The Project Technical Officer Must Demonstrate Alignment with GGGI’s mission and values of inclusivity, sustainability, and green growth. Ability to work effectively in a multicultural environment and build productive relationships with colleagues and stakeholders. Commitment to promoting an organizational culture of transparency, respect, and partnership. Ability to communicate clearly and collaborate with diverse teams to achieve project goals. Exhibit a proactive and problem-solving approach in addressing project-related challenges Regularly contribute to periodic technical and progress reports, which will be reviewed by the Executing Agency and UNEP to track delivery against outputs and timelines. Maintain project management structures, including oversight will be guided through coordination with the GGGI Technical Quality Assurance Expert, thematic working groups, and project steering committees where progress and performance are regularly reviewed. Manage the project’s monitoring and evaluation arrangements, including the M&E table and annual reporting to the GEF, will track progress against planned deliverables These mechanisms collectively ensure adequate accountability and quality assurance of Project Technical Officer’s role. WORKING CONDITIONS This role is a G8 international grade level in GGGI's salary scale. For G8 International grade, the base salary starts from USD 76,080. Determination of base salary is subject to the candidate's experience, academic background, and internal equity. GGGI provides 15% of base salary towards retirement plan/long-term savings, 27 days of annual leave, and private health insurance that covers dental and vision. GGGI is committed to providing a work environment that is sufficiently flexible to accommodate diverse life-cycle challenges and assist Staff members to achieve a better balance between work and personal/family commitments, thus ensuring high performance, long-term productivity, and well-being of Staff members. Child protection – GGGI is committed to child protection, irrespective of whether any specific area of work involves direct contact with children. GGGI’s Child Protection Policy is written in accordance with the Convention on the Rights of the Child.
